{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#thm-hoeffding}
#### Hoeffding's inequality

Let $X_1, \ldots, X_n$ be [IID](independence.qmd#def-iid) [random variables](random-variables.qmd#def-random-variable) with $X_i \in [0, 1]$ and [population mean](expectation.qmd#def-expectation) $\mean$,
and let $\samplemean{X}{n} \eqdef \avgin X_i$.
Then for every $\tolout > 0$
[@wikipedia_hoeffdings_inequality],

$$
\Prf{\samplemean{X}{n} - \mean \ge \tolout} \le e^{-2n\tolout^2}.
$$ {#eq-hoeffding-one-sided}

:::

::: proof

Let the free parameter be $s > 0$.
The event $\set{\samplemean{X}{n} - \mean \ge \tolout}$ is the event $\set{e^{sn(\samplemean{X}{n} - \mean)} \ge e^{sn\tolout}}$,
because the exponential is increasing and $sn > 0$.
The random variable $e^{sn(\samplemean{X}{n} - \mean)}$ is positive,
so [Markov's inequality](#thm-markov) applies:

$$
\ba
\Prf{\samplemean{X}{n} - \mean \ge \tolout}
&= \Prf{e^{sn(\samplemean{X}{n} - \mean)} \ge e^{sn\tolout}}
&& \text{(the exponential is increasing)} \\
&\le e^{-sn\tolout} \E{e^{sn(\samplemean{X}{n} - \mean)}}
&& \text{(Markov's inequality)}
\ea
$$

Rewrite the exponent as a sum, so that the exponential becomes a product:

$$
\ba
e^{sn(\samplemean{X}{n} - \mean)}
&= e^{s\sumin (X_i - \mean)}
&& \text{(} n\samplemean{X}{n} = \sumin X_i \text{)} \\
&= \prod_{i=1}^n e^{s(X_i - \mean)}
&& \text{(} e^{a + b} = e^{a} e^{b} \text{)}
\ea
$$

The factors are functions of independent random variables,
so they are independent,
and the expectation of a product of independent random variables is the product of their expectations
(the [expectation of a product of independent variables](variance-covariance.qmd#thm-indpt-uncorrelated), applied one factor at a time).
Then apply @lem-hoeffding to each factor:

$$
\ba
\E{e^{sn(\samplemean{X}{n} - \mean)}}
&= \prod_{i=1}^n \E{e^{s(X_i - \mean)}}
&& \text{(independence)} \\
&\le \prod_{i=1}^n e^{s^2/8}
&& \text{(Hoeffding's lemma)} \\
&= e^{ns^2/8}
&& \text{(} n \text{ equal factors)}
\ea
$$

Combining the two displays, for every $s > 0$,

$$
\Prf{\samplemean{X}{n} - \mean \ge \tolout} \le e^{-sn\tolout + ns^2/8}.
$$

The right side is smallest where the exponent $-sn\tolout + ns^2/8$ is smallest.
The exponent is a quadratic in $s$ with a positive leading coefficient, so it has one minimum, where its derivative is zero.
Its derivative in $s$ is $-n\tolout + ns/4$,
which is zero at $s = 4\tolout$, and $4\tolout > 0$ is allowed.
There the exponent is

$$
\ba
-4\tolout \cdot n\tolout + \frac{n(4\tolout)^2}{8}
&= -4n\tolout^2 + 2n\tolout^2
&& \text{(substitute } s = 4\tolout \text{)} \\
&= -2n\tolout^2
&& \text{(combine like terms)}
\ea
$$

which is the claim.

:::
